title: The Gang Goes to a Water Park

jokes.text: Charlie in a racing swimsuit explaining aerodynamics to uninterested gang members
jokes.setup: Charlie is wearing a racing suit to a water park and assumes everyone is curious about it
jokes.punchline: "No, not even a little bit" — the gang is completely indifferent, undercutting Charlie's self-importance
jokes.explanation: Perfect Charlie energy — delusional self-importance, complete misreading of the room, and the flat denial from the gang is well-timed. Very character-specific; only Charlie would prep for a water park with race aerodynamics.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Oh, Christ, does every single one of these kids have the flu?

jokes.text: "You're like, 'What's that rascal Charlie up to? What's he up to this time?' Right, right?" / "I'm not thinking that at all."
jokes.setup: Charlie imagines the gang is fascinated by his racing suit and narrates their supposed inner monologue
jokes.punchline: Dennis flatly denies having any such thought
jokes.explanation: "That rascal Charlie" is a brilliantly specific piece of self-narration — Charlie imagines himself as a folk hero protagonist in his own story. The deadpan denial lands hard. Highly quotable phrase that encapsulates the character perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: You're like, 'What's that rascal Charlie up to?' 'What's he up to this time?' Right, right?

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I'm not thinking that at all.

jokes.text: "The brochure says three days. We're saying bullshit to that. One day."
jokes.setup: The gang is planning their water park day
jokes.punchline: Charlie treats riding every slide in a water park in one day as a serious athletic/logistical challenge worthy of defying the official brochure
jokes.explanation: The absurdity of treating a water park brochure like a mountain-climbing challenge guide is funny and very on-brand for Charlie's delusional competitiveness.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: You're like, "What's that rascal Charlie up to?" "What's he up to this time?" Right, right?

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I'm not thinking that at all.

jokes.text: "You got, like, ten minutes of clean water and then every slide's basically a urine delivery system."
jokes.setup: Mac enthusiastically declares they're going to ride every ride
jokes.punchline: Dennis immediately reframes the entire water park as a urine delivery infrastructure with clinical detachment
jokes.explanation: "Urine delivery system" is an exceptional piece of phrasing — clinical, specific, and deeply unromantic about a place that's supposed to be fun. High economy, memorable phrasing. One of the stronger lines in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Yeah, the brochure says three days.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: We're saying bullshit to that. We're gonna get it done in one.

jokes.text: "We're not gonna get drenched in piss." / "No." — Mac and Dennis's plan to find one favorite ride and sit by the pool disease-free
jokes.setup: Mac declares their plan is to find one ride and avoid disease
jokes.punchline: Dennis immediately points out the water is already "infested with every parasite on the planet" — their plan is delusional from the start
jokes.explanation: Decent setup for the irony that all their plans will fail, but it's functional rather than exceptional. The foreshadowing is a bit on-the-nose.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: ten minutes of clean water and then every slide's basically a urine delivery system

jokes.text: Frank's reason for coming to the water park: "Hot food, cold beer, bikini'd women seeking relief from the insufferable prison of motherhood."
jokes.setup: Someone asks Frank why he even comes to a water park if he won't get in the water
jokes.punchline: Frank's answer is a perfectly cynical and predatory breakdown of what a water park actually offers — not fun, but vulnerable divorced mothers
jokes.explanation: "The insufferable prison of motherhood" is a legitimately great line — dark, specific, and captures Frank's predatory worldview with elegant economy. It's also a perfect setup for Dennis's parallel subplot with the fake daughter con. Only Frank could say this with such cheerful matter-of-factness. One of the strongest lines in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Hot food, cold beer, bikini'd women seeking relief from the insufferable prison of motherhood

jokes.text: "It's all free, too, if you know how to get it." / "Well, it's not free, you got to pay to get in." / "Not me, I had my bracelet laminated in the '90s. I haven't paid to get in here since I was 14."
jokes.setup: Frank cryptically implies he gets everything free at the water park
jokes.punchline: His method is a laminated wristband from the 1990s — an absurdly committed long-term scheme that reveals he's been doing this for decades
jokes.explanation: The reveal of a laminated wristband from the '90s is a beautiful piece of Frank worldbuilding — it's specific, it's committed, and it implies he has been running low-level scams for literally 25+ years. The gang's appreciative "Nice!" reaction adds to it.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Uh, it's a urine tester. Just want to be 100% sure. It turns light red at the slightest hint of piss.

jokes.text: Mac's pre-park warning: "Do not go near the pool drains, no matter how good you might think they feel on your butt."
jokes.setup: The gang is about to rush in as the park opens
jokes.punchline: Mac spontaneously warns everyone not to sit on the pool drains due to butt-suction — specifically qualifying it with "no matter how good you might think they feel"
jokes.explanation: The qualifier "no matter how good you might think they feel" is the key — it implies personal experience and raises disturbing questions about Mac's past. The gang's baffled reactions sell it perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Not me, I had my bracelet laminated in the '90s. I haven't paid to get in here since I was 14.

jokes.text: "Those things will suck the intestines right out of you. Like it did to that one kid back in '96. Now, she had to chew through her intestines just to get free."
jokes.setup: Mac is warning about pool drains
jokes.punchline: He cites a specific 1996 incident where a child had to chew through her own extruded intestines to escape a drain — presented as established fact
jokes.explanation: This is exceptional dark absurdism — the specificity of 1996, the clinical description of the child chewing through her own intestines, and Mac's matter-of-fact delivery make this a standout. It's also set up as a callback payoff later (Sherman/bracelet scene), showing structural planning. Genuinely disturbing and hilarious.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Shut up, nerd!

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Screw you, nerd!

jokes.text: Charlie produces a vial that tests water for urine — "It turns light red at the slightest hint of piss."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee arrive at the Kiddie Twister slide
jokes.punchline: Charlie has prepared a DIY urine-detection vial, treating the water park like a scientific expedition requiring field testing equipment
jokes.explanation: The piss-testing vial is a perfect Charlie prop — it's both paranoid and weirdly competent. It also serves as a running gag prop that pays off brilliantly later in the slide sequence. The color-change system is a lovely bit of absurd worldbuilding.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Do not go near the pool drains, no matter how good you might think they feel on your butt

jokes.text: "Slide's for kids only. Size requirement." / "Shut up, nerd!" (all adults pile onto kiddie slide)
jokes.setup: A park employee points out the slide is for kids only
jokes.punchline: The gang collectively dismisses him as a "nerd" and piles onto a children's slide anyway
jokes.explanation: Calling the safety attendant a "nerd" and ignoring him is classically Sunny — the gang treating rules as personal affronts from lesser people. Functional and in character, sets up the stuck-in-slide consequence perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Those things will suck the intestines right out of you. Like it did to that one kid back in '96. Now, she had to chew through her intestines just to get free.

jokes.text: Mac and Dee get stuck in the kiddie slide — "I'm stuck, wait!" / "Yeah, no shit!"
jokes.setup: Adults ignore the size restriction and pile onto a children's water slide
jokes.punchline: Exactly what the nerd warned about happens — Mac and Dee get jammed together in the slide
jokes.explanation: The setup-and-consequence is well-structured — the nerd was right, and the gang's immediate disaster is satisfying. The "Yeah, no shit!" from Dee is the right beat. The humor here is more situational than witty.

dialogue.line: Getting stuck in the kiddie slide together

jokes.text: "Some big, fat kid's just gonna come blasting down on us."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee are stuck and trying to stay calm
jokes.punchline: Mac's catastrophizing immediately focuses on the most viscerally unpleasant possible outcome — being hit by a heavy child at speed
jokes.explanation: Good foreshadowing beat that pays off immediately with a thud. The specificity of "big, fat kid" is a bit cheap but functional within the show's sensibility.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: I can't ever tell which way is north on a map.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: It's at the top.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: I thought north was, like, up.

jokes.text: (thud) — a child blasts into Mac and Dee in the slide, immediately after Mac predicts exactly that
jokes.setup: Mac says "some big, fat kid's just gonna come blasting down on us"
jokes.punchline: Immediately: thud, both yell
jokes.explanation: Perfect comic timing — the setup and payoff are literally seconds apart. The speed of the callback is what makes it work. Pure structure, almost no craft needed beyond placement. High impact in the room.

dialogue.line: Oh, Ethan is here with a special program for children with leukemia, so he skips to the front of the line.

jokes.text: Charlie can't tell which direction is north on a map — "I thought north was, like, up." / "'Up'?" / "Yeah, like if I turn the map this way, now where is north?" / "Still at the top of the—no." / "Down?"
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie are lost navigating the water park with a map
jokes.punchline: Charlie's confusion about north reveals he doesn't understand maps at a fundamental level — he thinks rotating the map changes north's location
jokes.explanation: This is excellent Charlie-specific comedy. The reveal that he thinks rotating the map relocates north is a perfect expression of his functional illiteracy applied to spatial reasoning. Frank's baffled "'Up'?" and Charlie's sincere "Down?" follow-up are beautifully structured escalation. Only Charlie.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: AIDS! AIDS, I got AIDS. I got AIDS, we're coming through.

jokes.text: Child with leukemia skips to the front of the line via special program
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie are annoyed at being stuck in a slow line, then see someone cutting
jokes.punchline: The line-cutter is a child with leukemia using a special program — which Frank immediately decides to exploit
jokes.explanation: The reveal that the line-skip is for kids with leukemia is perfectly timed — it immediately triggers Frank's exploitation instinct, which is very on-brand. Good structural beat that pays off in the AIDS scheme.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: He got it from a gay guy in the '80s.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I'm not gay, I didn't...

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: There's two kind of AIDS... there's the vagina AIDS and then the needle-based AIDS.

jokes.text: "He got it from a gay guy in the '80s. I'm not gay, I didn't—" / "Well..." / "There's two kinds of AIDS — there's the vagina AIDS and then the needle-based AIDS. I'm a vagina guy."
jokes.setup: Frank is performing AIDS illness to cut the line; Charlie improvises as his "doctor"
jokes.punchline: Frank's attempt to disavow gay AIDS spirals into an increasingly specific taxonomy of AIDS types, with Charlie undercutting him at every turn
jokes.explanation: The escalation here is superb — Frank's panic about being perceived as gay leads him to invent "vagina AIDS" and "needle-based AIDS" as medical categories, while Charlie keeps contradicting his diagnosis. It's simultaneously dark, absurd, and character-specific. Frank's sexuality anxiety is a recurring character note that makes "I'm a vagina guy" extra funny in context.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Let a little sunshine back into her life ever since her mom...

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Oh, my God. Did she...

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Die horrifically?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Drowning. Kind of ironic, us being at a water park

jokes.text: "Well, no, actually my test results show I got — sorry, I'm — AIDS. That it was the gay AIDS." / "All AIDS are bad." / "Well..." / "That's — no good AIDS."
jokes.setup: Charlie is posing as Frank's doctor while Frank insists he doesn't have gay AIDS
jokes.punchline: Charlie, as "doctor," keeps accidentally diagnosing Frank with the gay AIDS anyway, then retreats to "all AIDS are bad" as a diplomatic cover
jokes.explanation: "All AIDS are bad" as the diplomatic medical opinion of a fake doctor is a great line. Charlie's fumbling of his own role — repeatedly diagnosing Frank with gay AIDS after Frank explicitly protests — is excellent improv-style escalation comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Abby
dialogue.line: Can I please have $20?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Well, I think you can get something to eat for a lot less than that, hon.

dialogue.speaker: Abby
dialogue.line: Dad! I'm hungry, I'm starving, and you haven't given me any money.

jokes.text: "Lie back down." — scene cut to Frank performing sick in a water park chair
jokes.setup: The AIDS scam is in progress; Frank presumably sat up or broke character
jokes.punchline: Charlie's terse "Lie back down" implies they are actively staging a sickbed performance in the middle of a water park
jokes.explanation: Perfect economy — three words imply a full visual scene of Frank performing terminal illness on a pool lounger while Charlie stage-manages the con. The abruptness is the whole joke.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Interesting.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: What's interesting?

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Nothing. I'm done with you.

jokes.text: Dennis's pickup approach: inventing a dead wife / "Die horrifically?" / "Yeah. Drowning. Kind of ironic, us being at a water park..."
jokes.setup: Dennis spots a single mother at the water park and approaches with what appears to be a vulnerable widower story
jokes.punchline: The woman guesses the death was horrific; Dennis confirms it was drowning, then pivots to "you got to roll with the punches" — dark irony of using a drowning death to pick up women at a water park
jokes.explanation: The irony of invoking a drowning death at a water park as a seduction strategy is sharp and dark. The woman's immediate leap to "Die horrifically?" shows she's already primed to be manipulated, which is its own disturbing joke. Very Dennis — using real tragedy as a prop.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Sherman, did you pee?

dialogue.speaker: Sherman
dialogue.line: No.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Sherman, my vial is turning light pink.

dialogue.speaker: Sherman
dialogue.line: Ugh... goddamn it, Sherman, I ordered you not to pee!

jokes.text: "Interesting." / "What's interesting?" / "Nothing. I'm done with you. Keep up."
jokes.setup: Dennis observes Abby demanding money and behaving badly with the woman
jokes.punchline: Dennis dismisses the woman entirely and pivots his attention to Abby as a more interesting subject — treating a child's bad behavior as an audition
jokes.explanation: "I'm done with you. Keep up." is a great Dennis line — the abrupt dismissal of an adult woman in favor of a child he finds more strategically interesting captures Dennis's sociopathic prioritization perfectly. Very character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Don't question him; we need God!

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: God didn't put the sun anywhere. The sun stays still; the Earth moves around it.

jokes.text: Mac's piss vial turning light red while kids are laughing — "Sherman, did you pee?" / "No." / "Sherman, my vial is turning light pink." / "Sorry!"
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee are still stuck in the slide; Mac is monitoring the piss vial
jokes.punchline: The vial confirms what they feared — Sherman (a child) has peed on them in the slide
jokes.explanation: Perfect payoff for the vial setup — the scientific instrument is now confirming the worst in real time. Mac's formal reprimand of a child for peeing in a water slide is appropriately absurd. Good running gag execution.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: no matter how alluring it is, do not put your genitals or your butthole near the pool drain. You got it? In fact, cover your butthole.

jokes.text: Mac's piss-vial turns light pink as a kid named Sherman has peed in the slide while they're stuck
jokes.setup: Mac established his piss-testing vial earlier. They're stuck in the slide with children.
jokes.punchline: The vial turns pink — confirming what everyone feared. Mac furiously berates Sherman for peeing despite being ordered not to.
jokes.explanation: Good callback payoff for the vial setup. The specificity of Mac having ORDERED Sherman not to pee implies Mac gave this instruction to children earlier, off-screen, which is very funny. The vial going pink is exactly what it was designed to detect.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Mac. Stop talking to children about their buttholes, okay? It's not appropriate.

jokes.text: "Nobody else pee!" Mac orders the trapped children not to urinate
jokes.setup: Mac discovers Sherman has peed on them in the slide
jokes.punchline: Mac issues a formal command to a group of trapped children not to urinate — as if this is a matter of discipline rather than biology
jokes.explanation: The absurdity of treating urination as a matter of willpower and obedience is very funny, especially Mac's military-style delivery. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: That kid looks passed out, Dee.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: Yeah, he's out cold, but I think I can maneuver his body pretty easily.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Yeah, but if we send him down there, he might drown.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Guys, I gotta take a poop.

jokes.text: Dee and Mac argue about the sun — "Dee, if God put the sun there, there's probably a reason, okay? Don't question him; we need God!" / "God didn't put the sun anywhere. The sun stays still; the Earth moves around it."
jokes.setup: The sun is blasting Mac in the face while they're stuck in the slide
jokes.punchline: Mac's crisis invokes God's intentional sun placement; Dee corrects him with basic astronomy, which Mac cannot process
jokes.explanation: Classic Mac character comedy — his religious certainty applied to sun positioning during a crisis is very on-brand. "We need God!" while stuck in a kids' slide covered in urine is a great line. Dee's matter-of-fact astronomy correction is the right straight-man beat.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: Officer Dennis Reynolds. Hi. Off-duty, of course. This is your jurisdiction.

jokes.text: Mac to trapped child: "Before you go — no matter how alluring it is, do not put your genitals or your butthole near the pool drain. In fact, cover your butthole."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee manage to get one child out of the slide jam
jokes.punchline: In the moment of crisis management, Mac's priority is to pass on the pool drain warning to the escaping child
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback — in the middle of a physical crisis, Mac's first priority is the butthole-drain warning. "Cover your butthole, kid!" is a legitimately great line. The persistence of this fixation across the episode is both a running gag and a character revelation.

dialogue.speaker: Abby
dialogue.line: Try to touch me, and I'll scream 'rape.'

jokes.text: "That kid looks passed out, Dee." / "Yeah, he's out cold, but I think I can maneuver his body pretty easily." / "Yeah, but if we send him down there, he might drown."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee are trying to get children unstuck from the slide and spot an unconscious child
jokes.punchline: Dee's plan to "maneuver his body" is treated as a reasonable option; Mac's objection is only that the unconscious child might drown — not that using an unconscious child as a slide unblocker is wrong
jokes.explanation: Very dark — the casual consideration of sending an unconscious child down a waterslide, with the only objection being drowning logistics rather than ethics, is perfect Sunny darkness. Mac's pragmatic framing of the moral issue is well-executed.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: you want to be a thief or do you want to be an artist? You see, an artist takes whatever he wants when somebody's looking right at him.

jokes.text: "Guys, I gotta take a poop."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee are deep in crisis in the slide, debating the unconscious child
jokes.punchline: A child announces they need to defecate — the ultimate escalation of the bodily function situation
jokes.explanation: Perfect escalation beat — after urine, the natural next step is introduced. The placement immediately after the unconscious-child discussion is perfect timing. Pure economy; five words do all the work. The audience reaction to this in a crowd setting would be a big laugh.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: AIDS! Guy with AIDS, coming through.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Hey, man, go through.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: No, you need a raft! You need a raft!

jokes.text: Abby is caught shoplifting sunglasses: "I wasn't stealing them! I just forgot I was wearing them!" / "My dad's a cop!"
jokes.setup: Security catches Abby with stolen sunglasses
jokes.punchline: Abby's defense is the classic "forgot I was wearing them" excuse, then escalates to invoking a fake cop father as a threat
jokes.explanation: Good setup for Dennis's arrival — Abby's classic shoplifter excuses work because they're so familiar, and "my dad's a cop" lands as a knowing cliché. The humor is in recognizing the hustle.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: What are you guys doing? You guys doing a AIDS thing?

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Oh, yeah!

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: I gave Frank a couple hickeys to sell the lesions.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Sucked on 'em.

jokes.text: "Officer Dennis Reynolds. Hi. Off-duty, of course. This is your jurisdiction."
jokes.setup: Dennis arrives to handle Abby's shoplifting situation
jokes.punchline: Dennis introduces himself as a police officer to the security guard, with the qualifier "off-duty" — establishing a fake authority while deferring to the rent-a-cop in a move of calculated social maneuvering
jokes.explanation: "This is your jurisdiction" is a lovely piece of Dennis sociopathy — using procedural language to butter up a security guard he's actively deceiving. Very Dennis.

dialogue.speaker: Employee
dialogue.line: Oh, that's our new slide. It's, uh, Thunder Gun Express.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: Like the movie?

dialogue.speaker: Employee
dialogue.line: Yeah, but there's no water or anything yet, so we still have to test it. It's totally dry.

jokes.text: "Try to touch me, and I'll scream 'rape.'" — Abby to Dennis
jokes.setup: Dennis tells Abby she'll be "grounded for a month" as a performance for the security guard
jokes.punchline: Abby immediately threatens to scream rape if Dennis touches her — an extraordinary threat from a child that shows she's fully operating at Dennis's level of manipulation
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines in the episode. The shock of a child deploying this specific threat, completely unprompted, establishes Abby as a perfect mini-Dennis and immediately reframes the entire dynamic. Dennis's impressed silence is the correct reaction. Dark, specific, and perfectly economical.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: It's Thunder Gun, man. No hesitation. No surrender. No man left behind. We got to get to the top of that slide. And raw-dog the shit out of it!

jokes.text: "I see the road you're headed down: the lying, the stealing, all of it. And as somebody who's been down that road, let me tell you something: you've got real talent."
jokes.setup: Dennis lectures Abby about her bad behavior
jokes.punchline: What begins as a standard adult moral lesson flips entirely — Dennis's takeaway is that she's talented at being bad
jokes.explanation: Superb misdirection — the structure perfectly imitates a redemptive speech before detonating into the opposite. "You've got real talent" as the conclusion of a moral lecture is a great punchline. Very Dennis — he recognizes his own psychological profile in a child and responds with mentorship. High character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: My vial is blood red. That's because the water's not even running through anymore. It's just pooling up.

jokes.text: "You want to be a thief or do you want to be an artist? You see, an artist takes whatever he wants when somebody's looking right at him." — Dennis's lunch con
jokes.setup: Dennis explains the difference between petty theft and his preferred method
jokes.punchline: "An artist takes whatever he wants when somebody's looking right at him" — Dennis frames brazen manipulation/theft as a philosophical art form, superior to mere sneaking
jokes.explanation: One of the strongest lines in the episode. The thief/artist distinction is a genuinely clever piece of writing — it frames Dennis's sociopathy as aesthetic philosophy. Highly quotable, deeply character-specific (only Dennis would construct this self-aggrandizing framework for con artistry), and elegantly structured. It also sets up its own callback when Abby runs the con on Dennis himself.

dialogue.speaker: Dee
dialogue.line: The problem is it's already happening. I'm peeing on your shoulder right now. But I don't mean to, I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: It's warm.

jokes.text: "These are too small for me. Yeah. You get the point." — Dennis failed to steal a child's pair of sunglasses
jokes.setup: Dennis is demonstrating the "artist" con by stealing sunglasses
jokes.punchline: He stole children's sunglasses that don't fit his adult head, then has to awkwardly acknowledge this
jokes.explanation: Good deflation beat after Dennis's grand speech — the "artist" immediately fails at the practical level. The deadpan recovery is well-executed. Good pacing moment.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Oh, I peed as soon as we got in the slide.

dialogue.speaker: Sherman
dialogue.line: Me, too.

jokes.text: Frank and Charlie's AIDS-fueled water park montage — cutting lines with "AIDS! Coming through!" while riding rides and losing belongings
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie use AIDS claims to cut every line in the park
jokes.punchline: The montage shows them riding every slide in pure joy, cutting lines with increasingly confident AIDS announcements, while losing cameras and chains
jokes.explanation: The montage is well-constructed — the music choice (Ini Kamoze's "Here Comes the Hotstepper") against Frank screaming AIDS at a water park achieves a genuinely joyful absurdism. The escalation of their confidence and the growing collateral destruction (losing belongings) is well-paced.

dialogue.speaker: Mac
dialogue.line: Like the girl in the pool drain when she got her anus stuck, she chewed through her prolapsed anus and chewed herself to freedom.

jokes.text: "Oh, all of our chains! You know how hard it is to get all of our chains."
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie lose their belongings going down slides
jokes.punchline: Charlie's most pressing concern is that they've lost all of their chains — implying they were wearing multiple chains to a water park
jokes.explanation: "All of our chains" implies they arrived at a water park wearing several chains as jewelry — a small but perfect detail of Sunny's trashy character work. The phrasing "all of our chains" (plural and collective) is especially good.

dialogue.speaker: Abby
dialogue.line: I said I'd kiss him if he met me in the parking lot. Then I swiped his wristband, so he can't get back in.

jokes.text: "What are you guys doing? You guys doing a AIDS thing?" / "Oh, yeah!" / "I gave Frank a couple hickeys to sell the lesions. Sucked on 'em."
jokes.setup: Dennis runs into Frank and Charlie mid-AIDS scheme
jokes.punchline: Dennis immediately recognizes the AIDS con as a standard scheme, and Charlie casually reveals he gave Frank hickeys to simulate Kaposi's sarcoma lesions by sucking on his skin
jokes.explanation: "Sucked on 'em" is a great reveal — Charlie cheerfully describes giving Frank hickeys as medical prop work. The normalcy with which Dennis processes "AIDS thing" as a recognizable scheme type also implies they've done variations of this before. Good character-specific detail.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: When I was your age, I couldn't have accomplished half the things you did today. See, this is why the Chinese are destroying us. If you were born in China, you'd be the head of some factory by now. Or they would've thrown you in a river, 'cause you weren't a boy.

jokes.text: Mac shouts 'Stop sending kids, nerd! You goddamn nerd!' at the slide operator who is still sending children down
jokes.setup: The slide operator (nerd) has been sending children down the slide that Mac and Dee are stuck in.
jokes.punchline: Mac, in a completely desperate situation of his own making, still has the energy to berate the nerd doing his job correctly.
jokes.explanation: Callback to the 'nerd' insult from the beginning. Mac's continued hostility toward the employee who was completely right about the size requirement is a satisfying character consistency joke. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Dennis
dialogue.line: I don't have a daughter.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.line: Yes, you do. The girl that was just...

jokes.text: "You doing a fake daughter thing?" / "Yeah." / "Cool. All right, man, see ya." (Dennis immediately starts fake crying)
jokes.setup: Dennis and Charlie briefly compare schemes
jokes.punchline: Dennis says "see ya" and immediately starts fake crying as he walks away — snapping directly back into his con performance
jokes.explanation: The instantaneous switch from casual gang check-in to fake crying performance is a great visual/character beat. It treats con artistry as a totally mundane activity, like a salesman returning to a sales call. The "Cool. All right, man, see ya" farewell before the crying snap is perfectly timed.

dialogue.line: Dennis realizing he's been conned by Abby

jokes.text: "We did it! Every single ride in here!" / "We won!" / "Hey! Suck on that, river rat!" — Frank and Charlie celebrating
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie complete their goal of riding every ride in one day
jokes.punchline: Their victory celebration is completely unhinged — "Suck on that, river rat!" shouted at an unnamed enemy, treating a water park achievement as a competitive triumph
jokes.explanation: "Suck on that, river rat!" is a pleasingly bizarre victory cry. The joy of the celebration and the specificity of the insult (river rat? why?) make it charming. Good energy.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: Oh, it burns! It burns! It burns! It burns! Aah! My back!
That guy has AIDS!

jokes.text: "Thunder Gun Express" — an unopened slide named after the in-universe pornographic film; "Like the movie?" / "Yeah, but there's no water or anything yet" / "No hesitation. No man left behind. We got to get to the top of that slide. And raw-dog the shit out of it!"
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie discover a new, unopened slide just as they've completed all the existing rides
jokes.punchline: The slide is named Thunder Gun Express (a reference to a beloved in-universe porno) and is dry/under construction, but Charlie insists they "raw-dog the shit out of it" regardless
jokes.explanation: "Raw-dog the shit out of it" applied to a dry concrete waterslide is a great line. The Thunder Gun reference rewards longtime viewers. Charlie's complete refusal to acknowledge that a dry slide is not a water slide captures his beautiful delusion. This sets up the catastrophic payoff.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: They should've sent a poet.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.line: All right, let's go, let's go.

jokes.text: "It's warm." — Mac's response to Dee peeing on his shoulder
jokes.setup: Dee announces she is actively urinating on Mac's shoulder
jokes.punchline: Mac's response is simply "It's warm" — a purely sensory observation that is somehow worse than any outburst would have been
jokes.explanation: Two words that do an enormous amount of comedic work. The understatement is perfect — a full outburst would be expected; a clinical sensory report is horrifying and therefore hilarious. The delivery would land as one of the biggest laughs of the episode in a room. Perfect economy score.

dialogue.speaker: Frank
dialogue.line: There's AIDS blood in the pool!
That's goddamn AIDS blood?!
Has anyone seen my son?
Goddamn it! I hate this goddamn water park!

jokes.text: "Oh, I peed as soon as we got in the slide." / "Me, too." — the children reveal they've been peeing the whole time
jokes.setup: Mac is furious at Dee for peeing; the kids laugh
jokes.punchline: The children casually reveal they peed immediately upon entering the slide — Mac and Dee have been soaking in children's urine the entire time, rendering the piss-vial testing utterly futile
jokes.explanation: Perfect structural payoff — the piss vial, the "nobody else pee" command, and all of Mac's monitoring have been completely pointless because the kids peed immediately. The children's cheerful laughter while Mac and Dee are covered in urine is a great cringe beat. The "Me, too" from a second child is devastating escalation. One of the best structural payoffs in the episode.

jokes.text: Mac's callback to the intestine girl: "Sherman can chew through it! Like the girl in the pool drain when she got her anus stuck, she chewed through her prolapsed anus and chewed herself to freedom."
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee need to get the laminated bracelet off to escape; Mac can't rip it
jokes.punchline: Mac's solution is inspired by the pool drain girl who chewed through her extruded intestines — now rendered as a "prolapsed anus" variant — and proposes Sherman chew through the bracelet the same way
jokes.explanation: Exceptional callback — the intestine girl from the opening has now become Mac's inspirational problem-solving template. The story has also mutated (now it's a "prolapsed anus" rather than just intestines), implying Mac's mythology grows in the retelling. Using a child named Sherman to chew through a wristband based on this logic is perfect absurdist escalation. High structural score for the payoff on an early-episode plant.

jokes.text: "Chew like you've never chewed before. Go, Sherman, chew!"
jokes.setup: Mac is trying to get Sherman to gnaw through a laminated wristband
jokes.punchline: Mac delivers an inspirational rallying cry for a child to chew through plastic, with the intensity of a sports coach
jokes.explanation: "Chew like you've never chewed before" is a great line — the sports-coach intensity applied to a child gnawing on a wristband is perfectly absurd. Good economy and energy.

jokes.text: Abby's wristband con — "I got some boy to give me this. I said I'd kiss him if he met me in the parking lot. Then I swiped his wristband."
jokes.setup: Abby returns to Dennis having solved the problem of needing a wristband
jokes.punchline: Abby ran a sexual-promise con on a boy to steal his wristband — a scheme that is both impressive and deeply troubling coming from a child
jokes.explanation: Abby running a promise-and-ditch con on a boy to steal his wristband is both impressive hustle and very dark for a child. It mirrors Dennis's own manipulation tactics perfectly, cementing her as his protégé. The specificity of leaving him waiting in the parking lot is an especially cruel detail.

jokes.text: "A genius whose fate is controlled by an idiot?" / "You think I'm a genius?" / "If you were born in China, you'd be the head of some factory by now. Or they would've thrown you in a river, 'cause you weren't a boy. All right, it's not a great analogy."
jokes.setup: Dennis is trying to inspire Abby not to be controlled by her mom
jokes.punchline: His inspirational China analogy detours into "or they would've thrown you in a river" — then he self-corrects by admitting it's "not a great analogy"
jokes.explanation: The pivot from inspirational speech to "or they would've thrown you in a river" is excellently dark, and Dennis's self-aware "it's not a great analogy" shows just enough self-awareness to make it funnier. Classic Dennis self-correction without actual remorse.

jokes.text: Dennis: 'That's a disappointing glimpse into your future' when Abby says she has to leave because her mom says so
jokes.setup: Abby is being called away by her mother — a normal parental authority figure.
jokes.punchline: Dennis frames a child obeying her parent as a profound character flaw and 'disappointing glimpse into her future.' His total inversion of normal adult-child power dynamics.
jokes.explanation: Dennis's worldview distilled: obedience to authority (even parental) is weakness. That a child obeying her parent is a 'disappointing glimpse into her future' is a great character-specific inversion. Very Dennis.

jokes.text: "Thanks, Dennis. For being the first adult to actually give a shit about me." — Abby's sincere moment
jokes.setup: Dennis has mentored Abby in con artistry and given her his wristband
jokes.punchline: Abby's sincere gratitude to Dennis — a sociopath who has been teaching her to steal, lie, and manipulate — as the first adult who "gives a shit" is deeply dark irony
jokes.explanation: The genuine emotional beat landing in a context of pure manipulation is very Sunny — the show's darkness often comes from characters almost touching real feeling while doing terrible things. Dennis's visible conflict (then the reveal she ran the con on him) makes this retroactively excellent.

jokes.text: Dennis approaches Abby's 'mother' to give a speech about Abby deserving better — the woman has no idea who Abby is: 'I don't have a daughter.'
jokes.setup: Dennis, believing he is championing Abby's cause, goes to confront her neglectful mother.
jokes.punchline: The woman has no daughter. The child Dennis spent the episode with used him completely — the 'mom called her' was just an exit strategy. Dennis has been out-conned by a child.
jokes.explanation: The reveal that the 'mom' doesn't know Abby is the full payoff of the Dennis storyline. Abby used a random woman as an exit cover story. Dennis — who prides himself on seeing through people — was completely played by a child he was 'mentoring.' The structure is excellent: Dennis's narcissism (going to confront the 'neglectful mother') is the trap that lands the punchline. Dennis being unable to process this ('Yes, you do. The girl that was just...') is perfect character comedy.

jokes.text: Flashback/replay: "Please take it." / "So you never forget me." / "An artist takes whatever he wants when somebody's looking right at him."
jokes.setup: Dennis has just discovered Abby stole his wristband
jokes.punchline: The show cuts back to show us Abby executing the exact "artist" con Dennis described, while his own words play over the moment she steals from him
jokes.explanation: The best structured moment in the episode. Replaying Dennis's own manifesto over the moment he's victimized by it is perfect ironic payoff. Dennis literally narrates his own defeat. The structure — teach the lesson, have it used against you, replay the lesson over the crime — is excellent screenwriting. Near-perfect on structure and earned_vs_cheap because it's entirely built from planted material.

jokes.text: Frank sliding down the dry Thunder Gun slide — the squeaking of skin on dry fiberglass, then screaming: 'Oh, it burns! It burns! It burns! It burns!'
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie decide to 'raw-dog' the dry, unfinished slide despite having no water
jokes.punchline: Frank goes down and immediately suffers the agonizing friction burns of dry skin on a fiberglass slide — his screaming escalates as he descends
jokes.explanation: Perfect consequence comedy — their bravado ('raw-dog the shit out of it') is immediately punished by physics. The squeaking sound effect plus escalating screaming is a great audio-visual gag. Frank's elderly body on a dry fiberglass slide is a viscerally funny image.

jokes.text: Frank and Charlie at the Thunder Gun dry slide — "They should've sent a poet."
jokes.setup: Frank and Charlie are looking at the Thunder Gun Express slide in reverence
jokes.punchline: "They should've sent a poet" — Charlie appropriates this phrase (from Contact/popular culture) to describe a water park slide, with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: "They should've sent a poet" applied to a water park slide with complete sincerity is a great Charlie line — it captures his capacity for genuine wonder at completely mundane things. It also works as an unexpected cultural reference that lands because of the earnestness. Very quotable.

jokes.text: "Oh, it burns! It burns! It burns!" — Frank sliding down a dry concrete waterslide
jokes.setup: Frank goes down the unfinished Thunder Gun slide
jokes.punchline: Without water, sliding down concrete causes severe friction burns, which Frank announces in agony
jokes.explanation: The payoff for the dry slide setup is satisfying and well-timed. Frank's screaming is funny but relatively predictable given the setup. The real comedy comes from what happens next.

jokes.text: Frank crashes into the pool — someone shouts 'That guy has AIDS!' leading to mass panic and pool evacuation
jokes.setup: Frank crashes into the pool, injured and covered in what looks like injuries from the dry slide. The 'AIDS' scam has been running all day.
jokes.punchline: Someone in the crowd recognizes Frank as the AIDS patient from earlier — leading to screaming about 'AIDS blood in the pool' and total mass evacuation.
jokes.explanation: Perfect episode climax — the AIDS scam that Frank and Charlie used all day comes back as a catastrophic consequence. Frank crashing into the pool and someone recognizing him as 'the AIDS guy' causes mass panic and clears the entire park. The scam succeeds so hard it destroys the water park. 'There's AIDS blood in the pool!' being screamed as everyone evacuates is a great earned callback payoff. High structure score because this is the entire AIDS plot coming to its natural conclusion.

jokes.text: Frank lands in an empty pool and crowd thinks it's AIDS blood — "There's AIDS blood in the pool!" / "That's goddamn AIDS blood?!"
jokes.setup: Frank crashes into the pool bleeding from slide injuries; he still has the AIDS hickeys/branding
jokes.punchline: The crowd, seeing a bleeding man who was loudly claiming AIDS all day, panics that there is AIDS blood in the pool — triggering a mass evacuation
jokes.explanation: Perfect episodic payoff — the AIDS scheme, the dry slide, and Frank's injuries all collide into one catastrophic consequence that empties the entire water park. The structure is excellent: plant the AIDS claim early, let it run through the episode as a successful con, then have it cause maximum chaos at the climax. "That's goddamn AIDS blood?!" from a panicked bystander is a great crowd reaction line. Among the best-structured moments in the episode.

jokes.text: Mac and Dee are freed from the slide by the mass pool evacuation: "We're free! Oh, my God! We're free!"
jokes.setup: Mac and Dee have been stuck in the kiddie slide for the entire episode
jokes.punchline: The Frank/AIDS chaos clears the park, which apparently also resolves the slide jam — Mac and Dee are liberated by collateral chaos
jokes.explanation: The two plots resolving each other is structurally satisfying — Frank's AIDS scheme inadvertently saves Mac and Dee. The "We're free!" celebration after spending an entire episode covered in children's urine is a great cathartic beat. Good convergence structure.

jokes.text: "I hate this goddamn water park!" — a random parent's final declaration as chaos reigns
jokes.setup: Total chaos: pool cleared for AIDS blood, children screaming, Frank bleeding
jokes.punchline: An unknown parent crystallizes everyone's experience with a simple, heartfelt statement
jokes.explanation: A good crowd-reaction button to end the chaos sequence. No character integration since it's a random person, but the timing is right and the economy is good. Functions as a Greek chorus moment.

jokes.text: Final man screaming 'I hate this goddamn water park!' over dramatic music as everyone evacuates
jokes.setup: Total chaos — pool cleared, people screaming about AIDS blood.
jokes.punchline: One man's completely personal and specific grievance ('I hate this goddamn water park!') against the backdrop of an AIDS panic is a funny note to end the climax on.
jokes.explanation: Minor punctuation joke on a big setpiece. The personal grievance amid chaos is a standard comedy device but executed competently. Not particularly original.

jokes.text: (trio chanting backwards) — closing scene
jokes.setup: Episode seemingly concludes after the water park chaos
jokes.punchline: Three of the gang are shown chanting backwards — a surreal non-sequitur tag with no explanation
jokes.explanation: Classic Sunny tag — a weird non-sequitur that intentionally doesn't explain itself. The humor is in the commitment to the bit and the refusal to explain. Works better on rewatch when the audience has context, but the initial impact is mild confusion-amusement. Characteristic of the show's willingness to end on pure absurdism.

tmdb_overview: The gang takes a trip to a local waterpark. Dennis takes on a protégé. Frank and Charlie are determined to ride every ride. Mac and Dee get stuck in a tube slide.
